To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the nonlocal gluon condensates contribute to the fermionic vertex in different ways depending on whether the zero point is set on the gluonic- or fermionic-line.

(1) the dimension-four gluonic condensate contributions in the three-point vertex with the gluon condensation can be derived by using the nonlocal two gluon vacuum expectation value; (2) the result with the fixed-point gauge and non-covariant nonlocal two-guon vev depends on the zero-point of the fermionic line; (3) the uncertainty can be avoided with the covariant nonlocal two gluons vev.
the dimension-four gluonic condensate contributions with different forms of nonlocal two gluon vev to the fermionic 3-point vertex are obtained in the fixed-point and covariant gauges.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dimension-four gluonic condensate contributions of the fermionic three-vertex in QCD.
the gluon condensation effect on the fermionic three-gluon vertex.
the gluonic condensate contributions with the nonlocal two gluon vev to the fermionic vertex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dimension-four gluonic condensate contributions are zero in the covariant gauge, and the result is gauge independent.
the nonlocal gluon condensates in the nonlocal two-point gluon vev can not be ignored in the study of fermionic vertex corrections.
the dimension-four gluonic condensate corrections are zero in the covariant gauge and the fixed-point gauge.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gluonic-line zero-point is the correct zero-point for the gluon condensation in the fermionic three point vertex.
the gluon condensation effect on the fermionic three-vertex can be described in the covariant form, and it is independent of the choice of the zero-point.
the gluonic-line zero-point should be set on the fermion-fermion-gluon vertex, and the fermionic-line zero-point on the gluon-gluon-fermion vertex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dimension-four gluonic condensate contributions with the gluon condensation in the nonlocal two gluon vev can be used to study the fermionic three point vertex.
, in contrast to the case of the fermion condensate, the gluon condensation does not contribute to the fermionic vertex in the covariant gauge.
the nonlocal gluon condensates can be used to study the three-point vertex of the quark-gluon coupling.
